namedCorpusNotAuthored: crash at every journal write/fsync/rename/pointer and migration prepare/commit/abort/no-return transition

classes.memberVerbatim: crash at every journal write/fsync/rename/pointer and migration prepare/commit/abort/no-return transition
classes.exactByteIntentVerbatim: Once authored: per D-002 platform, digest-pinned crash injections at every named journal write, fsync, rename, and pointer transition, and at every migration prepare, commit, abort, and no-return boundary. Each record retains the injected site, the pre-crash generation identity, the post-recovery observer-visible generation (old or new, never mixed), and whether recovery resumed or restored an exact verified generation or fail-closed/quarantined. This class names crash-injection sites. It does not choose an on-disk journal format, lock-file grammar, lease API, solver, filesystem layout, or reviewed-equivalent of atomic rename. Those mechanisms remain reserved. This specification does not apply lifecycle-generation-contract.v2. Repair-media crash injection remains joined through DR-G06, DR-G08, and DR-G11 and is not this class. Fixtures are unauthored.
classes.passPropertyVerbatim: After each named crash site, observers see generation N or generation N+1, never a mixture. Ambiguous bytes or state fail closed and quarantine. A skipped named site is not a waiver. Recovery does not invent a journal implementation, a D9/loss code, or a self-update. Pass all four D-002 platforms. Windows is not a cell.
classes.slashJoinerVerbatim: journal write/fsync/rename/pointer stays one injection family; migration prepare/commit/abort/no-return stays one injection family; the two families are joined by 'and' into one corpus class

classes.exactByteIntentVerbatim: Once authored: per D-002 platform, digest-pinned records of two projects concurrently selecting incompatible component/artifact closures (file 04: different projects may concurrently select conflicting component versions). Each record retains both lock pin-sets (signed index snapshot, component/artifact closure, platform alternative, subprotocol/state formats, and policy constraints as file 04 names them) and proves generations do not mix. This class is cross-project conflicting locks. It does not invent a same-project concurrent-analyze class, a live-lease activation class, or a two-cache-writer class. It does not execute G16 lock-lane results. It does not fork DR-103 lockSchema and does not produce a lock. Window meaning of pinned format identifiers remains DR-111. Fixtures are unauthored.
classes.passPropertyVerbatim: Two projects may hold incompatible closures at the same time. A process leased to generation A cannot observe generation B's bytes as if they were A's. Mixing fails. Waiver of a mixed generation is not a skipped cell. Pass all four D-002 platforms.

classes.exactByteIntentVerbatim: Once authored: per D-002 platform, digest-pinned process-death records during a journaled lifecycle operation. Each record retains the held lease/refcount, the death event, lease reap (explicit or process-death reaped), and fail-closed recovery of the generation pointer. This class is generation/lease crash-safety. It is not G21 component process-tree kill/reap, not G09 grant-linearization process death, and not G12 doctor crash/backup/external-store cases. Fixtures are unauthored.
classes.passPropertyVerbatim: A dead process's lease is reaped. Ambiguous generation state fails closed. Uncommitted publication is not visible as a mixture. G21, G09, and G12 are not scored here. Pass all four D-002 platforms.
